liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Doll** (4 reviews): Described as one of the most beautiful things the reviewer has heard; China Doll is named among the most notable moments of the show [28][29][32][34]
- **Morning Dew** (4 reviews): Reviewer singles out Morning Dew emerging from Space as a reason to get the show; Morning Dew out of Space is among the most notable moments for this reviewer [28][29][30][36]
- **Bertha** (1 review): The opener is explained as a response to the pre-show rainstorm and arrests outside [27]
- **Althea** (1 review): At 7:45 it is shorter than the June, July and August 1985 versions but very strong [33]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Fun version, with classic Jerry and Brent vocals at the end [31]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer hears cool effects during Estimated [31]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Jerry's picking is sharp, especially in the second solo [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-11-02.171787.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 149 min [1]
- **gd1985-11-02.senn421.zaleski.ford.91238.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 147 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [7]. Said about its sound: Bass distortion during Morning Dew appears on every recording of this show [7]
- **gd85-11-02.sbd.jim.14604.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 134 min; rated 4.21/5 by 39 [17]. Said about its sound: Good quality, though lineage question marks suggest one or two analog generations; still sounds sweet when turned up; Reviewer calls the soundboard sound the best, with high energy [28][31]
- **gd85-11-02.aud-oade.remaster.20663.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 142 min; rated 4.44/5 by 18 [23]. Said about its sound: Of three sources heard, this audience recording best captures the room's vibe and is about as good as audience gets; This audience version captures the ambiance of the room well; Audience tape's tone captures what was coming off the stage; band played sweetly and flowing [29][30][32]

## Around the show

- Last Grateful Dead show at the Richmond Coliseum; the band was banned afterward following many arrests in a rainstorm before the show [27]
- The show took place amid bad weather and police hassles [36]
- Reviewer counts this among favorite 1985 Altheas, about a minute shorter than the 6/22, 7/14 and 8/31 versions [33]
- Overshadowed by the previous night's show but worth hearing [34]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-11-02.171787.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [1]
- **gd1985-11-02.senn421.zaleski.ford.91238.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Lucien Zaleski; transferred by Alex Ford; source: MAC; 2 x Sennheiser 421 > Sony D5 > D5 > Maxell XLII-S 90 (Set I) Maxell MX 90 (Set II). [7]
- **gd85-11-02.sbd.jim.14604.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > ? > DAT > CD > EAC > WAV > CoolEdit2000 (retracking) >SHN [17]
- **gd85-11-02.aud-oade.remaster.20663.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Oade Bros.; transferred by Doug Oade; source: Schoeps CMC441s (90deg, 17cm) + (CMC42 omni - offset ~ 8') > custom mixer made by Doug Oade (M118 circuit in a 3 channel package) > Oade mod SONY PCM-F1 [23]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by John Richards Grateful Dead: [1985-11-02 Richmond Coliseum, Richmond, VA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-11-02-richmond-coliseum-richmond-va-usa/) [40]

An unlisted Playin' jam comes out of China Doll into Drums
